attributes.body_ja:
「更（さら）に」は、副詞（ふくし）として「ますます」や「(A) よりもっと」といった意味（いみ）で使（つか）われる言葉（ことば）です。この語（ご）は漢字（かんじ）「更（さら）」が持（も）つ「新（あたら）しいものにする」という意味（いみ）をもとにしており、時間（じかん）・質（しつ）・量（りょう）のどれかに関（かん）して、最初（さいしょ）の状態（じょうたい）よりも進（すす）んでいることを表（あらわ）します。そのため、「(A) の上（うえ）に重（かさ）ねて」といった意味（いみ）も含（ふく）みます。

「さらに」は副詞（ふくし）として、基準（きじゅん）となる情報（じょうほう）が述（の）べられた後（あと）に、文（ぶん）の後半（こうはん）の始（はじ）めに使（つか）われることが多（おお）いです。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「更（さら）」の「新（あたら）しいものにする」という意味（いみ）は、すでに「いっぱい」である (A) に同（おな）じものをもっと加（くわ）えることで、そのものの状態（じょうたい）を変化（へんか）させる、というようなニュアンスを持（も）ちます。そのため、「さらに」を使（つか）った文（ぶん）では、(A) にそれだけで完全（かんぜん）または十分（じゅうぶん）な状態（じょうたい）が入（はい）り、(B) にそれを超（こ）えることが入（はい）ります。その結果（けっか）が肯定的（こうていてき）か否定的（ひていてき）かは、文脈（ぶんみゃく）によります。
attributes.body:
更（さら）に is word that is often used adverbially in Japanese to convey the meaning of 'more and more', 'even more than (A)', or 'again'. This use is an extension of the base meaning that the kanji 更（さら） has in indicating that something is 'approaching change'. Because of this, the expression used following 更（さら）に will always be something that is either further along than the initial statement either in regard to time, quantity, or volume. Taking this into consideration, 'in addition to (A)' may also be used as a fairly standard translation.

As さらに is used adverbially, it often appears at the beginning of part (B) of a sentence, after the 'base' information has already been indicated.

Fun-fact

The meaning of 更（さら） as 'approaching change' merely indicates that something has already reached 'fullness', and anything more than that will cause a fundamental change in the state of (A). Due to this, さらに primarily indicates things where (A) is considered 'complete' or 'enough' in and of itself, and what happens in (B) pushes that thing beyond a certain threshold. This may be either positive or negative depending on the sentence.

上に and 更に both add information, but their nuance differs. 上に connects additive facts or qualities, often with a static or descriptive tone, as in 彼は真面目な上に礼儀正しい (He is serious, and also polite). 更に emphasizes progression or intensification, as in 更に速く走った (He ran even faster).

attributes.body: その上 and 更に are both relatively formal expressions used at the beginning of a sentence to add information. While often interchangeable, they differ subtly: 更に can imply that the added point is of the same type as what came before, while その上 can highlight that the following point is particularly notable or worthy of emphasis.

attributes.body: Both add information, but differ in nuance. しかも emphasizes reinforcement or surprising addition, as in この料理はおいしい。しかも安い (This dish is delicious. And what’s more, it’s cheap). 更に is more formal, indicating progression or escalation, as in 明日は更に寒くなるでしょう (Tomorrow it will get even colder).

attributes.body: また is common in both speech and writing, meaning 'again' or introducing additional information, like 'moreover' or 'additionally'. 更に is more formal and used in writing or structured speech, with the nuance of 'even more' or 'beyond that', often indicating further change or escalation.

attributes.body: Both 再び and 更に can involve repetition or continuation, but they differ in meaning. 再び means 'again' or 'once more', and is used when something is done a second time after a pause, e.g. '再び会う' ('to meet again'). 更に means 'further' or 'more', and emphasizes intensification or accumulation, e.g. '更に深まる' ('to deepen further').

second_relatable.title: 更に

attributes.body: 更に and ますます both suggest addition or progression, but with different nuances. 更に emphasizes adding something on top of what already exists, e.g. '更に三人が参加した' ('Three more people joined'). ますます highlights a state intensifying over time, e.g. 'ますます寒くなってきた' ('It's gotten colder and colder').
